candidates.title: Lower learning rate
candidates.hypothesis: Reducing the learning rate from 3e-4 to 2e-4 improves distributional conformity without reducing chemical validity.
candidates.mechanism: Smaller updates may reduce late-epoch overfitting while preserving learned SMILES syntax.
support_criteria: Validity decreases by no more than 0.01.
candidates.information_value: Tests whether optimization step size is limiting generalization.

candidates.title: Higher dropout
candidates.hypothesis: Increasing dropout from 0.1 to 0.2 improves novelty while preserving distributional conformity.
candidates.mechanism: Stronger regularization may reduce memorization of training strings.
support_criteria: Conformity decreases by no more than 0.005.
candidates.information_value: Separates memorization effects from model-capacity effects.

candidates.title: Larger embedding dimension
candidates.hypothesis: Increasing the embedding dimension from 256 to 384 improves descriptor conformity by representing SMILES token contexts more effectively.
candidates.mechanism: A larger token representation may capture more structural context before attention layers.
candidates.information_value: Tests a model-capacity hypothesis that is independent of optimization and regularization.
